<script>
  // Restore the saved color scheme preference, or
  // enact the browser preference if "automatic", 
  // without expecting DOM load to have completed.
  //
  // Also restore any saved readingmode and ToC display preferences.
  function initializeReadingPreferences() {
    let saved_theme = localStorage.getItem("ar5iv_theme") || "automatic";
    if (saved_theme === "automatic") {
      if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
        saved_theme = "dark";
      }
    }
    if (saved_theme == "dark") {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    } else {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    }

    const tocDisplay = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_toc_display');
    if (tocDisplay) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-toc-display", tocDisplay);
    }
    const readingMode = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_reading_mode');
    if (readingMode) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-reading-mode", readingMode);
    }
  }
  // Run as soon as JS starts, to minimize repainting
  initializeReadingPreferences();
</script>

  /* Reading mode hides the chrome and the empty .arxiv-html-header marker: the pinned JS reads
     the marker's display to know which way to toggle. The marker draws no box. */
  .arxiv-html-header { display: contents; }
  html[data-reading-mode="enabled"] :is(.arxiv-html-site-chrome, .arxiv-html-header, .ds-site-footer) { display: none; }
  /* The paper controls' icons are blocks, so they sit centred (the pinned JS shows the theme
     icon by making its span a block). */
  .arxiv-html-site-chrome .ds-site-header-tools svg { display: block; width: 18px; height: 18px; flex-shrink: 0; fill: currentColor; }
  /* ar5iv dims every image in dark mode and puts it on a white wash, for paper figures;
     arXiv's own render as they are (the logo on the bar, the funder logos on their white
     chips). Important: ar5iv's dark rules are unlayered, as specific as
     :root:not([data-theme]) img:not(.ltx_no_dark_filter). */
  :is(.ds-site-header, .ds-site-footer) img { filter: none !important; }
  .ds-site-header img { background-color: transparent !important; }

  /* Wide (the theme's 1280px): the theme lays the body out as a grid whose full-width top rows
     were the band's and its sticky reader bar's. The band takes the first and scrolls away; the
     header, the paper's bar (no site navigation, the paper's controls), takes the second and
     stays in view, the one sticky bar, with the anchor clearance that requires (DESIGN-POLICIES).
     The controls show their names. */
  @media (min-width: 1280px) {
    html { scroll-padding-top: 80px; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome { display: contents; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome > #ds-announcement { grid-area: announce; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome > .ds-site-header { grid-area: header; position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: 3; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome .tool-icon { display: none; }
  }
  /* Narrow: the header scrolls away, and the controls show icons (names kept for screen
     readers; Why HTML? goes). The theme's contents panel is fixed below where its old sticky
     bar was, and hidden only once the reader has closed it, so until then it is an invisible box
     over the header and the paper: it shows only while open, under the chrome, in its place in
     the page. The paper's footer (build logs, reporting instructions) keeps the text's side
     inset; the theme gives it none, so it met the screen edges. */
  @media (max-width: 1279px) {
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome .tool-wide { display: none; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome .tool-label { position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; overflow: hidden; clip: rect(0 0 0 0); white-space: nowrap; }
    html:not([data-toc-display="block"]) .ltx_page_navbar { display: none; }
    .ltx_page_navbar { position: absolute; top: auto; }
    .arxiv-html-footer { padding-inline: 1rem; }
  }

<div id="p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="p1.1" class="ltx_p">[BoldFont=texgyretermes-bold.otf,ItalicFont=texgyretermes-italic.otf,BoldItalicFont=texgyretermes-bolditalic.otf]
[BoldFont=texgyreheros-bold.otf,ItalicFont=texgyreheros-italic.otf,BoldItalicFont=texgyreheros-bolditalic.otf]
[BoldFont=Inconsolatazi4-Bold.otf]</p>
</div>
<div id="p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2610.40577v2/band.svg" id="p2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/7;" width="476" height="7"></object>
</div>
<div id="p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="p3.pic1" class="ltx_picture" height="5147.24" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 1.38 5147.24" width="1.38"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,5147.24) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0) translate(0.69,0) translate(0,2573.65)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#F0F6FF;" fill="#F0F6FF"><path style="stroke:none" d="M -7.61 2573.62 L 7.61 2573.62 C 3.03 2573.62 -0.69 2569.9 -0.69 2565.32 L -0.69 -2565.32 C -0.69 -2569.9 3.03 -2573.62 7.61 -2573.62 L -7.61 -2573.62 C -3.03 -2573.62 0.69 -2569.9 0.69 -2565.32 L 0.69 2565.32 C 0.69 2569.9 -3.03 2573.62 -7.61 2573.62 Z M -0.69 -2573.62"></path></g><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 23.62 -3.46)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:-3.41em;--ltx-fo-height:183.69em;--ltx-fo-depth:183.19em;font-size:10pt;" height="5076.43" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 2541.68)" width="-47.18"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="p3.pic1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_top" style="width:-3.41em;">
<span id="p3.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p"></span>
<span id="p3.pic1.1.2" class="ltx_block ltx_align_left ltx_minipage ltx_align_middle" style="width:-34.1pt;"><span id="p3.pic1.1.2.1" class="ltx_ERROR undefined">\ErnieCoverFont</span>
<span id="p3.pic1.1.2.2" class="ltx_block ltx_minipage ltx_align_center ltx_align_middle" style="width:-30.7pt;"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2610.40577v2/wenxin_logo.svg" id="p3.pic1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:28/28;" width="28" height="28"></object>
<span id="p3.pic1.1.2.2.1" class="ltx_p ltx_align_center"><span id="p3.pic1.1.2.2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Multi-View Latent MoE:</span></span>
<span id="p3.pic1.1.2.2.2" class="ltx_p ltx_align_center"><span id="p3.pic1.1.2.2.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation</span></span>
<span id="p3.pic1.1.2.2.3" class="ltx_p ltx_align_center"><span id="p3.pic1.1.2.2.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Zelin Zhao<sup id="p3.pic1.1.2.2.3.1.1" class="ltx_sup"><math id="p3.pic1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\dagger" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>†</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\dagger</annotation></semantics></math></sup>, Junyuan Shang, Tianchi Ma,</span></span>
<span id="p3.pic1.1.2.2.4" class="ltx_p ltx_align_center"><span id="p3.pic1.1.2.2.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Shuohuan Wang<sup id="p3.pic1.1.2.2.4.1.1" class="ltx_sup">*</sup>, Dianhai Yu</span></span>
<span id="p3.pic1.1.2.2.5" class="ltx_p ltx_align_center"><span id="p3.pic1.1.2.2.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">ERNIE Team, Baidu</span></span>
<span id="p3.pic1.1.2.2.6" class="ltx_p"><span id="p3.pic1.1.2.2.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Abstract</span></span>
<span id="p3.pic1.1.2.2.7" class="ltx_p">Sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) models expand parameter capacity by activating only a small subset of experts for each token. Expert selection directly affects model capabilities under a fixed active-expert budget. However, dense evaluation of all experts reveals weak agreement between single-router score rankings and rankings from expert-utility evaluations, especially in middle and deep layers. Obtaining richer signals for selection and computation entails additional cost: selection based on internal expert activations requires preliminary computation, while processing multiple full representations separately through the same expert repeats its computation. We propose Multi-View Latent MoE to improve expert selection with multiple routers and further reuse their preferences to modulate expert computation under a fixed expert budget. Its Multi-Router submodule aggregates sigmoid scores from independently initialized routers. These routers develop highly differentiated expert preferences during training, allowing experts strongly favored by one router or jointly supported by several routers to be selected. Multi-View further uses each selected expert’s relative scores across routers to mix learned latent views into its input, reusing routing preferences for both selection and computation. Each selected expert executes one forward pass, preserving the active-expert count, expert FLOPs, and all-to-all communication volume. On a 24-layer 10B-A1B model trained on 708B tokens, full Multi-View Latent MoE improves the mean score across nine downstream tasks by 1.18 percentage points over the baseline. Its Multi-Router submodule alone yields a 0.6-percentage-point gain and improves the rank correlation between router scores and evaluated expert utility, with relative increases of 8.1% globally and approximately 58% in the layer with the lowest single-router alignment. Controlled mixing interventions further show that the model uses input differences that depend on both the expert and the token.</span>
<span id="p3.pic1.1.2.2.8" class="ltx_p"><span id="p3.pic1.1.2.2.8.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Oct 28, 2026</span></span>
</span>
</span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>

<figure id="S0.F1" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2610.40577v2/first_page_concept_en.svg" id="S0.F1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:476/390;" width="476" height="390"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 1: </span>Router-conditioned expert inputs in Multi-View. Equal total scores can express different preferences across routing heads and yield different mixed inputs. In this illustrative <math id="S0.F1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=2</annotation></semantics></math> example, experts <math id="S0.F1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S0.F1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math> have score pairs <math id="S0.F1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(0.4,0.1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(0.4,0.1)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S0.F1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(0.2,0.3)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(0.2,0.3)</annotation></semantics></math>, both summing to <math id="S0.F1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5</annotation></semantics></math>. Normalizing across routing heads for each expert gives view proportions <math id="S0.F1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(0.8,0.2)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.8</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(0.8,0.2)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S0.F1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(0.4,0.6)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.6</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(0.4,0.6)</annotation></semantics></math>, respectively. Routing heads and view projections read the same hidden state; each selected expert runs once. The balancing bias is set to zero. Shared experts, output gating, and up-projection are omitted.</figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">1 </span>Introduction</h2>

<figure id="S1.F2" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2610.40577v2/fig_intro_observation.png" id="S1.F2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/176;" width="476" height="176" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 2: </span>Agreement between single-router scores and empirical expert-utility evaluation on the 24-layer 10B-A1B backbone. <span id="S1.F2.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(a)</span> Spearman correlation across training. The logarithmic training-step axis expands the early stage and compresses later intervals to show early-training changes more clearly. <span id="S1.F2.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(b)</span> Layer-wise means over the 201 logged measurements used in the router comparison; shaded bands show <math id="S1.F2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm 1</annotation></semantics></math> standard deviation. Scores exclude the load-balancing bias. Expert utility is evaluated using each expert’s output <math id="S1.F2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>L</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> norm, normalized by its mean over sampled tokens (App. <a href="#A2.SS5" title="B.5 Router-score alignment ‣ Appendix B Experimental Details and Additional Analyses ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.5</span></a>).</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) models expand parameter capacity by activating a small subset of experts for each token <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shazeer et al., 2017</a>; <a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Fedus et al., 2021</a>)</cite>. This conditional computation enables larger language models under a limited active-computation budget. Routing scores determine which experts process each token and how their outputs are combined. The resulting capability depends on both expert selection and the computation performed by the selected experts.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Traditional MoE uses a single routing head followed by hard top-<math id="S1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> selection. Dense evaluation of all experts reveals limited agreement between the router’s ranking and the ranking obtained from empirical expert-utility evaluation, especially in middle and deep layers (Fig. <a href="#S1.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>). Unselected experts receive no direct task-loss gradient from that token, so poor selections may become self-reinforcing. This motivates assessing experts from multiple scoring perspectives rather than relying on one router.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Standard MoE uses routing scores to select experts and weight their outputs, but does not reuse them to construct expert inputs. Load-balancing methods regulate expert utilization <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2024a</a>)</cite>, but do not themselves provide multiple assessments of each expert. Activation-based routing such as AoE obtains expert-specific signals through partial evaluations of all experts, using low-rank factorizations to control the cost <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lv et al., 2025</a>)</cite>. Evaluating multiple input representations separately would also add expert computation. The challenge is therefore to obtain multiple assessments of experts and use routing preferences to modulate their computation while preserving the active-expert count, expert FLOPs, and communication volume.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">We propose Multi-View Latent MoE, a framework that reuses router preferences to improve expert selection and modulate expert computation. Its Multi-Router submodule combines multiple assessments of a shared expert pool: independently initialized sigmoid routing heads produce scores that are summed before one top-<math id="S1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> selection. These routers develop highly differentiated preferences during training. Their aggregation allows experts strongly favored by one router or jointly supported by multiple routers to be selected. This submodule retains a shared expert input while enriching the information used for selection.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Multi-View further uses these differentiated preferences to modulate each selected expert’s computation. The summed score alone does not retain the routers’ relative preferences: score vectors <math id="S1.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(0.4,0.1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(0.4,0.1)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S1.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(0.2,0.3)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(0.2,0.3)</annotation></semantics></math> both sum to <math id="S1.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5</annotation></semantics></math> but express opposite preferences (Fig. <a href="#S0.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>). Each router is paired with a learned latent projection, and each selected expert’s raw sigmoid scores are normalized across routers to blend the views into its input before evaluation. The projections are shared across experts, while the mixing proportions depend on both the token and the expert. Mixing takes place before dispatch, and each selected expert performs one forward computation, preserving the active-expert count, expert FLOPs, and all-to-all communication volume.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p6.1" class="ltx_p">On a 24-layer 10B-A1B model trained for 708B tokens, the full Multi-View Latent MoE improves the nine-task downstream mean by <math id="S1.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.18" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.18</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.18</annotation></semantics></math> percentage points over the baseline, reaching <math id="S1.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="34.25" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>34.25</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">34.25</annotation></semantics></math>; its Multi-Router submodule alone provides a <math id="S1.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.6</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.6</annotation></semantics></math>-point gain. Routing diagnostics show that this submodule improves global score–utility rank correlation by a relative <math id="S1.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8.1\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>8.1</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8.1\%</annotation></semantics></math>, with a relative gain of approximately <math id="S1.p6.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="58\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>58</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">58\%</annotation></semantics></math> in the layer with the lowest single-router alignment (§<a href="#S4.SS4" title="4.4 Alignment of router scores and expert outputs ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.4</span></a>). Measurements show distinct expert inputs for the same token. At the final MoE layer, permuting view-mixing proportions across experts while fixing expert selection and output gates raises held-out NLL by <math id="S1.p6.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.01340" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.01340</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.01340</annotation></semantics></math> nats/token; permutation across tokens for the same expert also increases NLL (§<a href="#S4.SS3" title="4.3 Router preferences shape expert computation ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.3</span></a>). These results show that the trained model uses the correspondence between mixing proportions, experts, and tokens.</p>
</div>
<section id="S1.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Contributions.</h4>

<div id="S1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<ul id="S1.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Multi-Router for improved expert ranking.</span> Dense evaluation of all experts reveals weak agreement between single-router score rankings and rankings from expert-utility evaluations, especially in middle and deep layers. Motivated by this observation, the Multi-Router submodule aggregates sigmoid scores from independently initialized routers. These routers develop highly differentiated expert preferences during training, and their aggregated scores achieve closer agreement with the evaluated utility rankings.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;padding-top:1.5pt;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Multi-View Latent MoE at a fixed expert budget.</span> The framework couples its Multi-Router selection submodule with router-conditioned latent-view mixing. Mixing before dispatch retains one forward computation per selected expert, the active-expert count, expert FLOPs, and all-to-all communication volume.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;padding-top:1.5pt;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Quantitative gains.</span> On a 24-layer 10B-A1B model trained for 708B tokens, full Multi-View Latent MoE improves the nine-task downstream mean by <math id="S1.I1.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.18" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.18</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.18</annotation></semantics></math> percentage points over the baseline; Multi-Router alone provides a <math id="S1.I1.i3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.6</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.6</annotation></semantics></math>-point gain. Multi-Router improves global score–utility rank correlation by a relative <math id="S1.I1.i3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8.1\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>8.1</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8.1\%</annotation></semantics></math>, with a relative gain of approximately <math id="S1.I1.i3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="58\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>58</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">58\%</annotation></semantics></math> in the layer with the lowest single-router alignment.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">2 </span>Related Work</h2>

<section id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Sparse MoE and expert specialization.</h4>

<div id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Sparse MoE layers route each token to a small subset of experts and combine their outputs <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shazeer et al., 2017</a>)</cite>. Token routing with a linear routing head and top-<math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> selection remains common in sparse MoE models <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cai et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">DeepSeek-AI et al., 2024b</a>; <a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jiang et al., 2024</a>)</cite>. Switch Transformer uses top-1 routing <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Fedus et al., 2021</a>)</cite>. Recent large language models also adopt MoE architectures <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">GLM-5-Team et al., 2026</a>; <a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2026a</a>)</cite>. Approaches such as fine-grained experts with an always-active shared expert increase the flexibility of expert specialization <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Dai et al., 2024</a>)</cite>. In these architectures, however, a discrete routing decision determines the active experts, which process a shared token representation.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Router design.</h4>

<div id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Router design addresses routing quality, stability, and load balance through methods including router <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math>-loss <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib45" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zoph et al., 2022</a>)</cite>, expert-choice routing <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhou et al., 2022</a>)</cite>, auxiliary-loss-free balancing <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2024a</a>)</cite>, mitigation of representation collapse <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chi et al., 2022</a>)</cite>, and attention over experts <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wu et al., 2024a</a>)</cite>. Expert assignments can fluctuate during training, motivating methods for more stable routing <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Dai et al., 2022</a>; <a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">Nguyen et al., 2025</a>)</cite>. Router Upcycling initializes query projections and expert keys from preceding attention layers for dense-to-MoE upcycling, then sums query–key matching scores across routers before softmax selection <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ran et al., 2025</a>)</cite>. MoR uses a learnable main router to weight sub-router outputs in LoRA expert mixtures for parameter-efficient fine-tuning <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib42" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al., 2025</a>)</cite>. Our Multi-Router submodule sums scores from separately parameterized sigmoid routing heads during pretraining. Multi-View further uses each expert’s relative scores across routing heads to construct its input.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Multi-representation and latent-space MoE.</h4>

<div id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A separate line of work changes the representations processed by experts. LatentMoE computes router scores from the full hidden state and evaluates experts in a low-dimensional latent space <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Elango et al., 2026</a>)</cite>. Stable LatentMoE modifies this design for training stability while retaining a single down-projection <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kimi Team et al., 2026</a>)</cite>. We build on this shared-projection architecture. MoLAE factorizes expert weights into shared latent mappings, optionally within expert groups, and expert-specific transformations <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2025b</a>)</cite>. AoE removes the separate router: experts are ranked by the <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>L</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> norms of their low-dimensional internal activations, and only selected experts continue computation; low-rank factorization reduces the cost of this initial evaluation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lv et al., 2025</a>)</cite>. MH-MoE splits projected tokens into sub-tokens that share a router and expert pool <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wu et al., 2024b</a>; <a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Huang et al., 2024</a>)</cite>. Multi-Head LatentMoE instead assigns each sub-token an independent MoE module with its own router and experts <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cui et al., 2026</a>)</cite>; SliceMoE also explores token slicing <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">Vejendla, 2025</a>)</cite>. MoH applies shared and routed components to attention heads rather than to the FFN <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jin et al., 2024</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Multi-View Latent MoE uses <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> projections of the full hidden state as a shared basis. For each selected expert, raw scores are normalized across routers to determine a token- and expert-dependent mixture before expert computation. The number of projections depends on <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math>, rather than on the number of experts, and expert parameters are shared across views. This changes the representation each expert receives. Prior analyses relate hidden-state geometry to expert-usage patterns <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2026b</a>)</cite>. Multi-Router retains the shared latent input of LatentMoE while aggregating multiple routing heads; Multi-View further reuses their preferences to modulate expert inputs.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3 </span>Method</h2>

<section id="S3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.1 </span>Preliminaries and framework overview</h3>

<div id="S3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We study autoregressive language modeling and modify the routing and expert-input interface of a latent-space MoE backbone <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Elango et al., 2026</a>)</cite>. The router reads the hidden state <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h\in\mathbb{R}^{D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>D</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h\in\mathbb{R}^{D}</annotation></semantics></math> and selects <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> routed experts. A down-projection <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times D}</annotation></semantics></math> supplies the shared input <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z=Ph" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z=Ph</annotation></semantics></math>. Each expert maps <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math>. With selected set <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}</annotation></semantics></math> and output gates <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, the latent expert aggregation is</p>
<table id="S3.E1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y=\sum_{i\in\mathcal{S}}g_{i}E_{i}(z)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi></mrow></munder><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y=\sum_{i\in\mathcal{S}}g_{i}E_{i}(z).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(1)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">The backbone up-projects this aggregation to dimension <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math> and combines it with the always-active shared-expert output.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Multi-View retains the shared expert pool and <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|\mathcal{S}|=k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\mathcal{S}|=k</annotation></semantics></math>, while reusing the preferences of individual routing heads for both selection and input construction. Its Multi-Router submodule aggregates scores; for each selected expert, scores normalized across routers mix latent views before one expert evaluation. Figure <a href="#S3.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 3.1 Preliminaries and framework overview ‣ 3 Method ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> shows the computation.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.F3" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2610.40577v2/multi_view_architecture_v6.svg" id="S3.F3.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/288;" width="476" height="288"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 3: </span>Comparison of latent-space MoE architectures. Top: (a) LatentMoE uses a router and a shared latent input; (b) Multi-Router sums scores from separately parameterized sigmoid routing heads for top-<math id="S3.F3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> selection while retaining the shared input; (c) Multi-View adds distinct down-projections and expert-specific view mixing. Bottom: expansion of the boxed routed path in (c), with matching colors and numbered markers. Balancing bias <math id="S3.F3.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>b</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math> is added to summed scores only for selection. Output gates <math id="S3.F3.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> follow Eq. <a href="#S3.E3" title="In 3.2 Multi-Router: score aggregation before selection ‣ 3 Method ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>. For each selected expert, raw sigmoid scores are normalized across routers to form view proportions <math id="S3.F3.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{m,i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{m,i}</annotation></semantics></math>, whose sum is one. Each selected expert processes its mixed input once. The aggregated representation <math id="S3.F3.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math> is up-projected and combined with the shared-expert output shown above. <math id="S3.F3.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=2</annotation></semantics></math> views and selected experts <math id="S3.F3.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i,j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i,j</annotation></semantics></math> are illustrative; <math id="S3.F3.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> is the number of active experts out of <math id="S3.F3.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math>. Bars depict example routing scores. Normalization modules and residual paths are omitted for clarity.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.2 </span>Multi-Router: score aggregation before selection</h3>

<div id="S3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Multi-Router uses <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> routing heads <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{w^{(r)}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msup><mi>w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{w^{(r)}\}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w^{(r)}\in\mathbb{R}^{D\times N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w^{(r)}\in\mathbb{R}^{D\times N}</annotation></semantics></math>, to score the shared expert pool from the full hidden state <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math>. Each routing head’s output passes through a sigmoid, and the resulting scores are summed before top-<math id="S3.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> selection:</p>
<table id="S3.E2" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_table">
<tbody>
<tr id="S3.E2X" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E2X.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\bar{s}_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>s</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\bar{s}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E2X.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\sum_{r=1}^{R}\sigma\!\big(w_{i}^{(r)\top}h\big)," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>R</mi></munderover></mstyle><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.437em;" width="0.437em"><mi>σ</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.222em">⊤</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\sum_{r=1}^{R}\sigma\!\big(w_{i}^{(r)\top}h\big),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="2" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equationgroup ltx_align_right">(2)</span></td></tr>
<tr id="S3.E2Xa" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E2Xa.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mathcal{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathcal{S}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E2Xa.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\mathrm{TopK}_{k}(\bar{s}+b)." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>TopK</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>s</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\mathrm{TopK}_{k}(\bar{s}+b).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.3" class="ltx_p">Here <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b\in\mathbb{R}^{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>N</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b\in\mathbb{R}^{N}</annotation></semantics></math> is the backbone’s expert-balancing bias, added only for selection. Output gates normalize the uncorrected score sums over the selected experts and apply the backbone’s routed-output scale:</p>
<table id="S3.E3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{i}=\alpha_{i}\frac{\bar{s}_{i}}{\sum_{j\in\mathcal{S}}\bar{s}_{j}},\qquad i\in\mathcal{S}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mfrac><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>s</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi></mrow></msub><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>s</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{i}=\alpha_{i}\frac{\bar{s}_{i}}{\sum_{j\in\mathcal{S}}\bar{s}_{j}},\qquad i\in\mathcal{S}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(3)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.4" class="ltx_p">Here <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> is the backbone’s learnable scalar for expert <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>; it scales the expert output, not the view mixture.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Routing heads are initialized with distinct seeds to break symmetry, without a diversity penalty. We use <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=2</annotation></semantics></math> by default. In Multi-View (§<a href="#S3.SS3" title="3.3 Multi-View: router-conditioned expert inputs ‣ 3 Method ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a>), each router is paired with one view, so <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=K</annotation></semantics></math> and the two symbols refer to the same count.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Summation after the sigmoid preserves the routing heads as distinct nonlinear scoring functions. Summing logits before the sigmoid instead gives a single linear scorer, since <math id="S3.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{r}w_{i}^{(r)\top}h=(\sum_{r}w_{i}^{(r)})^{\top}h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>r</mi></msub><mrow><msubsup><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.222em">⊤</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mo lspace="0em">∑</mo><mi>r</mi></msub><msubsup><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{r}w_{i}^{(r)\top}h=(\sum_{r}w_{i}^{(r)})^{\top}h</annotation></semantics></math>. Post-sigmoid summation lets a strong score from one routing head or support across routing heads affect the shared ranking and supplies the relative contributions used for input mixing. Alternatives and their properties appear in Apps. <a href="#A1.SS3" title="A.3 Choice of fusion position ‣ Appendix A Extended Method Discussion ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.3</span></a>–<a href="#A1.SS5" title="A.5 Aggregation before selection ‣ Appendix A Extended Method Discussion ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.5</span></a>, with training comparisons in §<a href="#S4.SS5" title="4.5 Training ablations ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.5</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.3 </span>Multi-View: router-conditioned expert inputs</h3>

<div id="S3.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Multi-View pairs <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> routing heads with <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> latent views in a one-to-one correspondence, so <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=K</annotation></semantics></math>. Selection and output gating follow the summed-score rules of Multi-Router, while each selected expert’s scores normalized across routers construct its input <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{v}_{i}=\sum_{m}a_{m,i}v^{(m)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>v</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>m</mi></msub><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>v</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{v}_{i}=\sum_{m}a_{m,i}v^{(m)}</annotation></semantics></math>. Views are fused before expert evaluation, and each selected expert runs once. This parameterization avoids evaluating experts separately for each view; for nonlinear <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, it is generally not equivalent to mixing outputs after separate evaluations:</p>
<table id="S3.Ex1" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S3.Ex1X"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.Ex1X.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle E_{i}\!\Big(\sum_{m}a_{m,i}v^{(m)}\Big)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">(</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mi>m</mi></munder></mstyle><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>v</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle E_{i}\!\Big(\sum_{m}a_{m,i}v^{(m)}\Big)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="S3.Ex1Xa"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.Ex1Xa.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\neq\sum_{m}a_{m,i}E_{i}(v^{(m)})." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo lspace="2.278em">≠</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mi>m</mi></munder></mstyle><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>v</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\neq\sum_{m}a_{m,i}E_{i}(v^{(m)}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Views.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We form <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> latent views <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v^{(m)}=P_{m}h\in\mathbb{R}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>v</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v^{(m)}=P_{m}h\in\mathbb{R}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math>, with each <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{m}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{m}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times D}</annotation></semantics></math> matching the shape of the backbone down-projection. View <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> uses the backbone’s projection <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>P</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P</annotation></semantics></math>; the remaining <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K{-}1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K{-}1</annotation></semantics></math> views use independently initialized perturbations, as described below. Each view projects the full hidden state rather than a subset of its channels. Expert architectures and input dimensions are unchanged.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Routing, mixing, and gating.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">All <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> routing heads read <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math>. Routing head <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math> produces <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{m,i}=\sigma(w_{i}^{(m)\top}h)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.222em">⊤</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{m,i}=\sigma(w_{i}^{(m)\top}h)</annotation></semantics></math> for every expert <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>, and these scores determine three operations.
<em id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">(i) Selection:</em> sum across routers, <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{s}_{i}=\sum_{m}s_{m,i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>s</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>m</mi></msub><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{s}_{i}=\sum_{m}s_{m,i}</annotation></semantics></math>, add the balancing bias, and take one top-<math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}=\mathrm{TopK}_{k}(\bar{s}+b)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>TopK</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>s</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}=\mathrm{TopK}_{k}(\bar{s}+b)</annotation></semantics></math>, as in Multi-Router.
<em id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">(ii) View mixing:</em> for each selected expert <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>, normalize its raw sigmoid scores across the <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> routing heads:</p>
<table id="S3.E4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{m,i}=\frac{s_{m,i}}{\sum_{n=1}^{R}s_{n,i}},\qquad\sum_{m=1}^{K}a_{m,i}=1,\quad i\in\mathcal{S}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>R</mi></msubsup><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo rspace="2.000em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>K</mi></munderover><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{m,i}=\frac{s_{m,i}}{\sum_{n=1}^{R}s_{n,i}},\qquad\sum_{m=1}^{K}a_{m,i}=1,\quad i\in\mathcal{S}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(4)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">These proportions form the convex mixture <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{v}_{i}=\sum_{m}a_{m,i}v^{(m)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>v</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>m</mi></msub><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>v</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{v}_{i}=\sum_{m}a_{m,i}v^{(m)}</annotation></semantics></math>. Neither the balancing bias nor the routed-output scale enters this mixture.
<em id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.2.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">(iii) Output gating:</em> use <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> from Eq. <a href="#S3.E3" title="In 3.2 Multi-Router: score aggregation before selection ‣ 3 Method ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> to combine the selected experts’ outputs. Thus, output gating normalizes summed scores over experts, whereas input mixing normalizes each expert’s scores across routers. The resulting expert aggregation is</p>
<table id="S3.E5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y=\sum_{i\in\mathcal{S}}g_{i}\,E_{i}\!\Big(\sum_{m}a_{m,i}\,v^{(m)}\Big)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi></mrow></munder><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">(</mo><mrow><munder><mo lspace="0em" movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mi>m</mi></munder><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>v</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y=\sum_{i\in\mathcal{S}}g_{i}\,E_{i}\!\Big(\sum_{m}a_{m,i}\,v^{(m)}\Big).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(5)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.3" class="ltx_p">Equivalently, the input uses a token- and expert-dependent effective projection,</p>
<table id="S3.Ex2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\mathrm{eff},i}(h)=\sum_{m}a_{m,i}(h)P_{m},\qquad\hat{v}_{i}=P_{\mathrm{eff},i}(h)h." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mrow><mi>eff</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mi>m</mi></munder><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>m</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>v</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mrow><mi>eff</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{\mathrm{eff},i}(h)=\sum_{m}a_{m,i}(h)P_{m},\qquad\hat{v}_{i}=P_{\mathrm{eff},i}(h)h.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.4" class="ltx_p">The projection basis <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{P_{m}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{P_{m}\}</annotation></semantics></math> is shared across experts; only its mixing coefficients depend on <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>. The implementation mixes the projected vectors, rather than materializing a separate matrix <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\mathrm{eff},i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>P</mi><mrow><mi>eff</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{\mathrm{eff},i}</annotation></semantics></math> for every token–expert pair.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Normalizing each expert’s scores across routers to derive the mixing weights requires no additional mixing network and makes view <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math>’s contribution to expert <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>’s input depend on the corresponding routing preference. Algorithm <a href="#alg1" title="Algorithm 1 ‣ Routing, mixing, and gating. ‣ 3.3 Multi-View: router-conditioned expert inputs ‣ 3 Method ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> gives the forward pass. Learned mixing weights and gradient coupling are evaluated in the corresponding ablation configurations in Section <a href="#S4.SS5" title="4.5 Training ablations ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.5</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="alg1" class="ltx_float ltx_float_algorithm ltx_framed ltx_framed_top">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_float"><span id="alg1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Algorithm 1</span> </span> Multi-View routed-expert branch forward pass</figcaption>
<div id="alg1.4" class="ltx_listing ltx_framed ltx_framed_topbottom ltx_listing">
<div id="alg1.l1" class="ltx_listingline">
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline">1:</span>
                
                
              hidden state <math id="alg1.l1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math>; projections <math id="alg1.l1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{P_{m}\}_{m=1}^{K}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>K</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{P_{m}\}_{m=1}^{K}</annotation></semantics></math>; routing heads <math id="alg1.l1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{w^{(m)}\}_{m=1}^{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msup><mi>w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>R</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{w^{(m)}\}_{m=1}^{R}</annotation></semantics></math>; experts <math id="alg1.l1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{E_{i}\}_{i=1}^{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{E_{i}\}_{i=1}^{N}</annotation></semantics></math>; active count <math id="alg1.l1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>; balancing bias <math id="alg1.l1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>b</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math>; routed-output scales <math id="alg1.l1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\alpha_{i}\}_{i=1}^{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\alpha_{i}\}_{i=1}^{N}</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
<div id="alg1.l2" class="ltx_listingline">
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline">2:</span>

</div>
<div id="alg1.l7" class="ltx_listingline">
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline">7:</span>

</span>

                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline">8:</span>
                
                
                <math id="alg1.l8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{v}_{i}\leftarrow\sum_{m}a_{m,i}\,v^{(m)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>v</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.111em" stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>m</mi></msub><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>v</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{v}_{i}\leftarrow\sum_{m}a_{m,i}\,v^{(m)}</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="alg1.l8.2" class="ltx_text" style="float:right;"><math id="alg1.l8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\triangleright" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>⊳</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\triangleright</annotation></semantics></math> per-expert view blend
</span>
</div>
<div id="alg1.l9" class="ltx_listingline">
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline">9:</span>
                
                
                <math id="alg1.l9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{i}\leftarrow\alpha_{i}\bar{s}_{i}/\sum_{j\in\mathcal{S}}\bar{s}_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>s</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em">/</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi></mrow></msub><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>s</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{i}\leftarrow\alpha_{i}\bar{s}_{i}/\sum_{j\in\mathcal{S}}\bar{s}_{j}</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="alg1.l9.2" class="ltx_text" style="float:right;"><math id="alg1.l9.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\triangleright" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>⊳</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\triangleright</annotation></semantics></math> output gate, Eq. <a href="#S3.E3" title="In 3.2 Multi-Router: score aggregation before selection ‣ 3 Method ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>
</span>
