                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline">11:</span>
                
                
              <span id="alg1.l11.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">return</span> <math id="alg1.l11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y=\sum_{i\in\mathcal{S}}g_{i}\,E_{i}(\hat{v}_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>v</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y=\sum_{i\in\mathcal{S}}g_{i}\,E_{i}(\hat{v}_{i})</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
</div>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Expert-dependent mixing weights.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The index <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math> in <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{m,i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{m,i}</annotation></semantics></math> allows input modulation to vary across experts. If all selected experts for the same token share <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{m,i}=a_{m}(h)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{m,i}=a_{m}(h)</annotation></semantics></math>, they receive the same input <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\big(\sum_{m}a_{m}(h)P_{m}\big)h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><msub><mo lspace="0em">∑</mo><mi>m</mi></msub><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>m</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\big(\sum_{m}a_{m}(h)P_{m}\big)h</annotation></semantics></math>. This remains token-conditioned modulation, but no longer distinguishes different experts for that token. If the weights are further fixed to constants, such as <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{m}=1/K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{m}=1/K</annotation></semantics></math>, the mixture can be absorbed into a fixed projection. Multi-View derives <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{m,i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{m,i}</annotation></semantics></math> from the raw scores for expert <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>, normalized across the <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> routing heads, making modulation depend on both the token and the expert (App. <a href="#A1.SS10" title="A.10 Properties: tied views and view differentiation ‣ Appendix A Extended Method Discussion ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.10</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Initialization.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To introduce the additional projections gradually, we retain the backbone down-projection for view <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> and parameterize the others as ramped perturbations, <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v^{(m)}=Ph+\gamma(t)\,\Delta P_{m}h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>v</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v^{(m)}=Ph+\gamma(t)\,\Delta P_{m}h</annotation></semantics></math>, with <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math> increasing from <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> early in training. At <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=0</annotation></semantics></math>, all view projections equal the backbone projection; after the ramp, the view projections are unconstrained. The expert inputs are weighted combinations of these views. This procedure can also initialize the views from an existing checkpoint (App. <a href="#A1.SS9" title="A.9 Warm-starting from a LatentMoE checkpoint ‣ Appendix A Extended Method Discussion ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.9</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Shared expert parameters.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">All views use one expert pool, so expert parameters are not duplicated or partitioned across views. Each selected expert processes one mixed input, and gradients propagate through every view with nonzero mixing weight. Multi-Router uses the shared input <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z=Ph" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z=Ph</annotation></semantics></math> for all selected experts; Multi-View adds input modulation through the router-derived coefficients (App. <a href="#A1.SS10" title="A.10 Properties: tied views and view differentiation ‣ Appendix A Extended Method Discussion ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.10</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Experiments</h2>

<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.1 </span>Setup</h3>

<div id="S4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We compare the latent-space MoE baseline, Multi-Router, and score-derived Multi-View on a 24-layer 10B-A1B backbone with top-8 routing and one always-active shared expert <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Elango et al., 2026</a>)</cite>. The three configurations share the training data, token budget, backbone, and optimization settings (App. <a href="#A2.SS2" title="B.2 The 10B-A1B configuration ‣ Appendix B Experimental Details and Additional Analyses ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.2</span></a>). Downstream evaluation uses the 708B-token checkpoints on nine tasks (protocol in App. <a href="#A2.SS4" title="B.4 Additional measurements ‣ Appendix B Experimental Details and Additional Analyses ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.4</span></a>). We use <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> for the number of routing heads and <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> for the number of views. The main method Multi-View(<math id="S4.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math>) pairs them one to one, so <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=K</annotation></semantics></math>; Multi-Router(<math id="S4.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math>) uses <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> routing heads with a shared expert input.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Training ablations examine router aggregation, learned input-mixing weights, and view-fed scoring. Their losses are averaged over a <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm 1\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>±</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm 1\%</annotation></semantics></math> token window around a common ablation checkpoint. A pair of near-matched runs differs after smoothing by at most <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.2\times 10^{-3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.2</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.2\times 10^{-3}</annotation></semantics></math>, with a mean absolute difference of <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="7\times 10^{-4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>7</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7\times 10^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math>. Architecture, optimization, and comparison settings are detailed in App. <a href="#A2.SS3" title="B.3 Comparability protocol ‣ Appendix B Experimental Details and Additional Analyses ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.3</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>

<td id="S4.T1.2.1.6.12" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t" style="--ltx-bg-color:#ECECEC;padding:0.4pt 3.5pt;"><math id="S4.T1.m15" class="ltx_Math" style="--ltx-bg-color:#ECECEC;" alttext="-0.34" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#ECECEC;" mathbackground="#ECECEC">−</mo><mn style="--ltx-bg-color:#ECECEC;" mathbackground="#ECECEC">0.34</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.34</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</tbody>
</table>
</span></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 1: </span>Downstream scores (%) at 708B training tokens. Baseline: latent-space MoE; MR: Multi-Router (<math id="S4.T1.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=2</annotation></semantics></math>); MV: score-derived Multi-View (<math id="S4.T1.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=R=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=R=2</annotation></semantics></math>; Eq. <a href="#S3.E5" title="In Routing, mixing, and gating. ‣ 3.3 Multi-View: router-conditioned expert inputs ‣ 3 Method ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>). Tasks are grouped into exams, knowledge, science, and reasoning. Avg. is the unweighted within-group mean; Overall is the unweighted mean across all nine tasks. Bold marks the highest displayed score in each column. The final row reports MV minus Baseline in percentage points. Prompt and scoring protocols appear in App. <a href="#A2.SS4" title="B.4 Additional measurements ‣ Appendix B Experimental Details and Additional Analyses ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.4</span></a>.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S4.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 4.2 Downstream performance ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> compares all three configurations at the same training budget. The nine-task means are <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="33.07" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>33.07</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">33.07</annotation></semantics></math> for the baseline, <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="33.69" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>33.69</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">33.69</annotation></semantics></math> for Multi-Router, and <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="34.25" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>34.25</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">34.25</annotation></semantics></math> for Multi-View. Multi-View improves the mean by <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.18" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.18</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.18</annotation></semantics></math> percentage points over the baseline and by <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.56" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.56</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.56</annotation></semantics></math> over Multi-Router. Gains over Multi-Router reach <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.74" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2.74</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.74</annotation></semantics></math> points on GPQA and <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.03" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2.03</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.03</annotation></semantics></math> on MMLU-Redux; CMMLU and MMLU improve by <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.43" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.43</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.43</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.17" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.17</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.17</annotation></semantics></math> points, respectively. These results indicate an aggregate benefit from extending selection with multiple routing heads to router-conditioned expert computation.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Training convergence.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#S4.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ Training convergence. ‣ 4.2 Downstream performance ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> compares the three configurations through the 708B-token checkpoint used for downstream evaluation. Over the final 1,000 steps, the mean losses are <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.25621" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2.25621</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.25621</annotation></semantics></math> for the baseline, <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.25047" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2.25047</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.25047</annotation></semantics></math> for Multi-Router, and <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.24883" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2.24883</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.24883</annotation></semantics></math> for Multi-View. Multi-Router reduces loss by <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5.74\times 10^{-3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>5.74</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5.74\times 10^{-3}</annotation></semantics></math> relative to the baseline, and Multi-View increases this reduction to <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="7.38\times 10^{-3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>7.38</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7.38\times 10^{-3}</annotation></semantics></math>. Multi-View’s lower loss in late training is consistent with its downstream gains.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.F4" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2610.40577v2/fig_loss_main.svg" id="S4.F4.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/210;" width="476" height="210"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 4: </span>Training loss of the baseline, Multi-Router, and Multi-View on 10B-A1B through 708B tokens. <span id="S4.F4.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(a)</span> Loss difference from the baseline; the inset shows the full loss trajectories. <span id="S4.F4.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(b)</span> Magnification of the blue-bordered window in (a), covering 50–230B tokens. <span id="S4.F4.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(c)</span> Magnification of the purple-bordered window in the full-loss inset, showing absolute loss over 620–708B tokens. All curves use the same causal exponential moving average (EMA), with a 2,000-step span (<math id="S4.F4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha=2/2001" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2001</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha=2/2001</annotation></semantics></math>), initialized at the first observation. The final losses reported in the text average the last 1,000 unsmoothed steps.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.3 </span>Router preferences shape expert computation</h3>

<figure id="S4.F5" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2610.40577v2/fig_mv_mechanism.svg" id="S4.F5.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/238;" width="476" height="238"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 5: </span>Expert-specific inputs and controlled mixing interventions in the score-derived Multi-View checkpoint at 708B tokens. <span id="S4.F5.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(a)</span> Differences among the eight experts selected for the same token: the mean absolute pairwise difference in view-1 proportions <math id="S4.F5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{r}</annotation></semantics></math> (top) and the mean pairwise input distance normalized by the mean input norm <math id="S4.F5.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{v}</annotation></semantics></math> (bottom). Zero denotes identical proportions or inputs, respectively. Curves show the median across tokens at each layer; bands show the 25th–75th percentiles. <span id="S4.F5.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(b)</span> Final-layer interventions on 256 sequences, changing view proportions while holding <math id="S4.F5.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}</annotation></semantics></math> and output gates <math id="S4.F5.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> fixed to numerical precision. Whiskers are 95% sequence-bootstrap CIs; crosses mark permutation-seed means. <span id="S4.F5.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(c)</span> Single-layer interventions on 80 sequences. Bands are pointwise 95% CIs; downstream routing is recomputed. <math id="S4.F5.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math>NLL is intervention loss minus the original loss.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S4.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We probe the score-derived Multi-View checkpoint used for downstream evaluation at 708B tokens. The analysis covers all 24 MoE layers on 256 held-out sequences of 4096 tokens. It examines expert-specific inputs and whether the trained model uses the correspondence between mixing proportions, experts, and tokens.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">From preferences to distinct expert inputs.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The two routing heads have markedly different rankings: across layers, their top-8 Jaccard index averages <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.145" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.145</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.145</annotation></semantics></math> and their top-1 agreement averages <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="11.2\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>11.2</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">11.2\%</annotation></semantics></math>. For each token, the probe exports the actual view-1 mixing proportion <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{1,i}=a_{1,i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{1,i}=a_{1,i}</annotation></semantics></math> and mixed input of each of its eight selected experts. We compare all 28 pairs of these experts: <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{r}</annotation></semantics></math> is their mean absolute proportion difference, and <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{v}</annotation></semantics></math> is their mean input distance divided by their mean input norm (App. <a href="#A2.SS6" title="B.6 Expert-input diversity and controlled mixing interventions ‣ Appendix B Experimental Details and Additional Analyses ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.6</span></a>). Both are zero when all eight experts receive the same proportions or inputs, respectively. Fig. <a href="#S4.F5" title="Figure 5 ‣ 4.3 Router preferences shape expert computation ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>(a) summarizes these within-token differences across tokens at each layer. The layer-wise medians are <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.27" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.27</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.27</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.46" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.46</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.46</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{r}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.42" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.42</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.42</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.58" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.58</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.58</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{v}</annotation></semantics></math>. The selected experts therefore receive distinct inputs according to their view preferences.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">The trained model uses the correspondence.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">At the final MoE layer, we hold the selected experts <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}</annotation></semantics></math> and their output gates <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> fixed to numerical precision and intervene only on the view-mixing proportions. For a replacement proportion <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{1,i}^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow><mo>′</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{1,i}^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math>, the two dispatcher channels are rebuilt as <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(g_{i}r_{1,i}^{\prime},g_{i}(1-r_{1,i}^{\prime}))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow><mo>′</mo></msubsup></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow><mo>′</mo></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(g_{i}r_{1,i}^{\prime},g_{i}(1-r_{1,i}^{\prime}))</annotation></semantics></math>, preserving their sum <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>. Permuting the view proportions among the selected experts of the same token raises NLL by <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.01340" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.01340</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.01340</annotation></semantics></math> nats/token (95% sequence-bootstrap CI: <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0.01256,0.01435]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0.01256</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.01435</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0.01256,0.01435]</annotation></semantics></math>). Using uniform mixing proportions <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(1/2,1/2)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(1/2,1/2)</annotation></semantics></math> raises NLL by <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.00662" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.00662</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.00662</annotation></semantics></math>; permuting proportions across tokens for the same expert raises it by <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.00223" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.00223</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.00223</annotation></semantics></math>. The respective CIs are <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0.00620,0.00709]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0.00620</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.00709</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0.00620,0.00709]</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0.00205,0.00241]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0.00205</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.00241</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0.00205,0.00241]</annotation></semantics></math>. Expert permutation increases sequence-average NLL for all 256 sequences. These interventions show that the trained checkpoint uses the correspondence between mixing proportions, experts, and tokens. Expert permutation produces the largest increase among these three interventions.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Both views contribute across depth.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Applying the view 1-only or view 2-only proportions at the final layer increases NLL by <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.01881" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.01881</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.01881</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.02042" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.02042</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.02042</annotation></semantics></math> nats/token, respectively. The trained checkpoint therefore uses both view branches. A separate 80-sequence scan perturbs one layer at a time: expert permutation and uniform mixing increase NLL, with pointwise 95% CIs above zero at all 24 layers. Only the intervened layer’s selections and output gates are fixed; subsequent routing is recomputed, so these are total effects including downstream responses. Additional preference, single-view, and token-group analyses appear in App. <a href="#A2.SS6" title="B.6 Expert-input diversity and controlled mixing interventions ‣ Appendix B Experimental Details and Additional Analyses ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.6</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.4 </span>Alignment of router scores and expert outputs</h3>

<figure id="S4.F6" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2610.40577v2/fig_oracle_alignment.svg" id="S4.F6.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/186;" width="476" height="186"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 6: </span>Router-score alignment with normalized expert-output norms. <span id="S4.F6.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(a)</span> Global Spearman correlation over training; solid curves use a 51-record moving mean and pale curves show raw measurements. <span id="S4.F6.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(b)</span> Layer-wise means and one-standard-deviation bands over 201 matched logged measurements; metric and aggregation definitions appear in App. <a href="#A2.SS5" title="B.5 Router-score alignment ‣ Appendix B Experimental Details and Additional Analyses ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.5</span></a>. <span id="S4.F6.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(c)</span> Correlation changes across all 24 layers. Multi-Router improves global correlation by a relative <math id="S4.F6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8.1\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>8.1</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8.1\%</annotation></semantics></math>, with the largest relative layer-wise gain of <math id="S4.F6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="57.7\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>57.7</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">57.7\%</annotation></semantics></math> at layer 20.</figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="S4.T2" class="ltx_table">

<tr id="S4.T2.2.1" class="ltx_tr">

<th id="S4.T2.2.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt" style="padding-left:8.0pt;padding-right:8.0pt;">Spearman <math id="S4.T2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ρ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho</annotation></semantics></math></th></tr>

<tbody class="ltx_tbody">
<tr id="S4.T2.2.2" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="S4.T2.2.2.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row ltx_border_t" style="padding-left:8.0pt;padding-right:8.0pt;">Single router</th>
<td id="S4.T2.2.2.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_t" style="padding-left:8.0pt;padding-right:8.0pt;"><math id="S4.T2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.1245" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.1245</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.1245</annotation></semantics></math></td></tr>

<th id="S4.T2.2.3.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:8.0pt;padding-right:8.0pt;">Multi-Router</th>
<td id="S4.T2.2.3.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:8.0pt;padding-right:8.0pt;"><math id="S4.T2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{0.1346}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold">0.1346</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{0.1346}</annotation></semantics></math></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 2: </span>Global alignment between pre-bias router scores and normalized expert-output norms, averaged over 201 matched logged measurements. Multi-Router improves rank correlation by a relative <math id="S4.T2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8.1\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>8.1</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8.1\%</annotation></semantics></math>. Definitions appear in App. <a href="#A2.SS5" title="B.5 Router-score alignment ‣ Appendix B Experimental Details and Additional Analyses ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.5</span></a>.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S4.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We compare the baseline and Multi-Router using the normalized expert-output norm. For each sampled token, all 256 experts process its latent input; each output’s <math id="S4.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>L</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> norm is divided by that expert’s mean norm over the sampled tokens. Spearman correlation measures agreement between the resulting expert ranking and the router scores before balancing bias (App. <a href="#A2.SS5" title="B.5 Router-score alignment ‣ Appendix B Experimental Details and Additional Analyses ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.5</span></a>). Related work also examines routing quality through expert-pathway optimization, routing-weight analysis, and expert-importance measurements <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2025a</a>; <a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2025b</a>; <a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2025c</a>; <a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2026</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S4.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 4.4 Alignment of router scores and expert outputs ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> reports an <math id="S4.SS4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8.1\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>8.1</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8.1\%</annotation></semantics></math> relative improvement in global rank correlation across 24 MoE layers, from <math id="S4.SS4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.1245" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.1245</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.1245</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S4.SS4.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.1346" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.1346</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.1346</annotation></semantics></math>. Figure <a href="#S4.F6" title="Figure 6 ‣ 4.4 Alignment of router scores and expert outputs ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> shows the training trajectories and layer-wise comparison, with gains in 17 of 24 layers. The largest relative gain occurs at layer 20, where correlation rises from <math id="S4.SS4.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.0625" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.0625</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.0625</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S4.SS4.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.0986" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.0986</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.0986</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="S4.SS4.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="57.7\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>57.7</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">57.7\%</annotation></semantics></math>); layer 7 shows the largest absolute gain, from <math id="S4.SS4.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.0982" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.0982</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.0982</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S4.SS4.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.1388" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.1388</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.1388</annotation></semantics></math>. These measurements show that aggregating differentiated routing heads improves alignment between router scores and normalized expert outputs, complementing the downstream and training-loss gains of Multi-Router.</p>
</div>
</section>

</span></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 3: </span>Multi-Router training ablations on 10B-A1B. Loss differences use the single-router baseline and a <math id="S4.T3.m25" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm 1\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>±</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm 1\%</annotation></semantics></math> token window around the common ablation checkpoint. All post-sigmoid aggregation operators reduce loss; the final row reports the observed run-pair difference.</figcaption>
</figure>

<td id="S4.T4.2.1.10.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><math id="S4.T4.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm 0.0012" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>0.0012</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm 0.0012</annotation></semantics></math></td></tr>

</table>
</span></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 4: </span>Input-mixing training ablations on 10B-A1B. The learned-weight variants use per-expert mixing parameters. In the view-fed coupling pair, both scoring and expert computation read the views; stopping the weight-to-view gradient increases loss by <math id="S4.T4.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.0114" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.0114</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.0114</annotation></semantics></math> while preserving forward weights at fixed parameters.</figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Fusion position and routing heads.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Multi-Router reduces loss by <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4.5\times 10^{-3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>4.5</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.5\times 10^{-3}</annotation></semantics></math> with two routing heads and <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5.1\times 10^{-3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>5.1</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5.1\times 10^{-3}</annotation></semantics></math> with three routing heads (Table <a href="#S4.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ 4.5 Training ablations ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>). The additional reduction of <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.6\times 10^{-3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.6</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.6\times 10^{-3}</annotation></semantics></math> is smaller than the observed run-pair difference of <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.2\times 10^{-3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.2</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.2\times 10^{-3}</annotation></semantics></math>. We use two routing heads by default. Fusion position determines whether the routing heads contribute distinct scoring functions: summing logits before sigmoid collapses them into one linear scorer (§<a href="#S3.SS2" title="3.2 Multi-Router: score aggregation before selection ‣ 3 Method ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2</span></a>), whereas applying sigmoid to each routing head before summation preserves their nonlinear contributions. The latter distinguishes equal-mean logits with different distributions across routing heads.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Fusion operators and routing-head contributions.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Different fusion rules determine how the scoring views contribute to expert selection. Maximum fusion retains only the strongest score, whereas products and geometric means emphasize joint support. Summation accumulates bounded contributions from all routing heads, allowing either a strong response from one routing head or support across routing heads to increase the aggregate. All evaluated fusion variants reduce loss by <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3.3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3.3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.3</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4.5\times 10^{-3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>4.5</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.5\times 10^{-3}</annotation></semantics></math> (Fig. <a href="#A2.F7" title="Figure 7 ‣ Training trajectories and aggregation operators. ‣ B.4 Additional measurements ‣ Appendix B Experimental Details and Additional Analyses ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>). The operator gaps lie within the observed run-pair difference. Beyond selection, Multi-View normalizes each selected expert’s raw scores across routing heads to construct input-mixing proportions (§<a href="#S3.SS3" title="3.3 Multi-View: router-conditioned expert inputs ‣ 3 Method ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a>), connecting selection with multiple routing heads to router-conditioned expert computation.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Learned input mixing.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S4.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ 4.5 Training ablations ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> compares three learned per-expert mixing parameterizations: symmetric initialization at <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5</annotation></semantics></math>, asymmetric initialization, and two independent gates. They reduce loss by <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4.4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4.4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.4</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5.0\times 10^{-3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>5.0</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5.0\times 10^{-3}</annotation></semantics></math> relative to the baseline while retaining the same active-expert budget. The main Multi-View method instead derives mixing weights directly from router scores, reusing the selection signal without an additional mixing network.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Gradient coupling in view-fed scoring.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A separate ablation feeds the views into both the scoring and expert-computation paths. Stopping the gradient from mixing weights to views changes the loss difference from <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.0024" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.0024</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.0024</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.0090" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.0090</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.0090</annotation></semantics></math>, an increase of <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.0114" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.0114</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.0114</annotation></semantics></math>. The forward weight values at fixed parameters are preserved, isolating the benefit of this gradient path within the view-fed configuration.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.6 </span>Parameter and computational efficiency</h3>

<section id="S4.SS6.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Parameter overhead.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For the 24-layer 10B-A1B backbone with two routing heads, the Multi-Router submodule adds approximately <math id="S4.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.06\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.06</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.06\%</annotation></semantics></math> parameters. Multi-View adds one latent-view projection per layer, contributing a further <math id="S4.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.13\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.13</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.13\%</annotation></semantics></math>, for a total increase of approximately <math id="S4.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.19\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.19</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.19\%</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS6.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Expert computation and communication.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Each selected expert processes one mixed input, preserving the active-expert count and activated expert FLOPs. Input mixing takes place on the source device before dispatch; each token still sends <math id="S4.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> vectors of dimension <math id="S4.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math>, preserving all-to-all communication volume. Additional work comes from routing, projection, and input mixing; for fixed <math id="S4.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math>, the extra scoring and projection cost scales as <math id="S4.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D(d+N)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D(d+N)</annotation></semantics></math>. Appendix <a href="#A1.SS6" title="A.6 Cost accounting in detail ‣ Appendix A Extended Method Discussion ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.6</span></a> gives the parameter and operation counts, together with same-cluster throughput measurements for the router and view-fed ablation configurations.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Multi-View Latent MoE reuses routing preferences to improve expert selection and shape expert computation. Motivated by weak agreement between single-router rankings and empirical expert-utility rankings, its Multi-Router submodule combines independently initialized routing heads that learn highly differentiated preferences. Routing diagnostics show relative rank-correlation gains of <math id="S5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8.1\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>8.1</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8.1\%</annotation></semantics></math> globally and approximately <math id="S5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="58\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>58</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">58\%</annotation></semantics></math> in the layer with the lowest single-router alignment. Multi-View further uses each selected expert’s relative scores across routing heads to blend latent views into its input before dispatch. Each selected expert runs once, preserving the active-expert count, expert FLOPs, and all-to-all communication volume. On a 24-layer 10B-A1B model trained for 708B tokens, full Multi-View Latent MoE improves the nine-task downstream mean by <math id="S5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.18" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.18</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.18</annotation></semantics></math> percentage points over the baseline; its Multi-Router submodule alone provides a <math id="S5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.6</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.6</annotation></semantics></math>-point gain. Controlled mixing interventions show that the model makes effective use of expert- and token-dependent input differences. These findings establish routing preferences as a signal for both selecting experts and shaping how they process each token.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="Sx1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section">Limitations</h2>

<div id="Sx1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The experiments use a 24-layer 10B-A1B backbone with a shared training seed and evaluate nine downstream tasks at the 708B-token checkpoint. The controlled interventions measure the trained model’s use of view mixing at that checkpoint.</p>
</div>
</section>

<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>Extended Method Discussion</h2>

<div id="A1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This appendix provides supporting analyses for the main-text method. Algorithm <a href="#alg1" title="Algorithm 1 ‣ Routing, mixing, and gating. ‣ 3.3 Multi-View: router-conditioned expert inputs ‣ 3 Method ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> in §<a href="#S3.SS3" title="3.3 Multi-View: router-conditioned expert inputs ‣ 3 Method ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a> gives the forward pass of the Multi-View routed-expert branch.</p>
</div>
<section id="A1.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.1 </span>LatentMoE as the backbone</h3>

<div id="A1.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Because the experts operate in latent space, replacing a selected expert’s input <math id="A1.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math> with a view <math id="A1.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v^{(m)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>v</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v^{(m)}</annotation></semantics></math> leaves its architecture, width, and hyperparameters unchanged. The existing expert blocks can therefore be reused without increasing expert capacity. Latent-space designs have also been studied in other MoE architectures <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Elango et al., 2026</a>; <a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2025b</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.2 </span>Contextual representations and expert inputs</h3>

<div id="A1.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Attention produces a contextual representation <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math>, but the baseline MoE still evaluates all <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> selected experts at the same projected input <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z=Ph" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z=Ph</annotation></semantics></math>. The attention representation and the expert inputs are separate architectural choices: multiple projections can give the selected experts different inputs derived from the same <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math>. We use the term <em id="A1.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">view</em> for this learned latent projection or the resulting expert input.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.3 </span>Choice of fusion position</h3>

<div id="A1.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We consider three positions for combining <math id="A1.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> router scores. <em id="A1.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">(1) Before the nonlinearity (logit sum):</em> <math id="A1.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{r}w_{i}^{(r)\top}h=(\sum_{r}w_{i}^{(r)})^{\top}h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>r</mi></msub><mrow><msubsup><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.222em">⊤</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mo lspace="0em">∑</mo><mi>r</mi></msub><msubsup><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{r}w_{i}^{(r)\top}h=(\sum_{r}w_{i}^{(r)})^{\top}h</annotation></semantics></math> is equivalent to a single scorer with weights <math id="A1.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{r}w_{i}^{(r)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>r</mi></msub><msubsup><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{r}w_{i}^{(r)}</annotation></semantics></math> (§<a href="#S3.SS2" title="3.2 Multi-Router: score aggregation before selection ‣ 3 Method ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2</span></a>). <em id="A1.SS3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">(2) After the sigmoid (ours):</em> each router first applies its own nonlinearity, after which the resulting scores are combined. <em id="A1.SS3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">(3) After normalization into probabilities:</em> each router’s scores are normalized before summation, removing differences in their overall scale. Table <a href="#S4.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ 4.5 Training ablations ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> reports the corresponding training comparisons.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.4 </span>Choice of fusion operator</h3>

<div id="A1.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For post-sigmoid fusion, different aggregation operators emphasize different score patterns. Let <math id="A1.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{m}\in(0,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{m}\in(0,1)</annotation></semantics></math> denote one router’s score for an expert. An additive operator, <math id="A1.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{m}s_{m}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>m</mi></msub><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>m</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{m}s_{m}</annotation></semantics></math>, allows a high score from one router to increase the aggregate even when other scores are low. Multiplicative operators, <math id="A1.SS4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\prod_{m}s_{m}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mo>∏</mo><mi>m</mi></msub><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>m</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\prod_{m}s_{m}</annotation></semantics></math> and the geometric mean <math id="A1.SS4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\prod_{m}s_{m})^{1/R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mo lspace="0em">∏</mo><mi>m</mi></msub><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>m</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>R</mi></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\prod_{m}s_{m})^{1/R}</annotation></semantics></math>, suppress an expert when any router assigns it a near-zero score. We also consider additive operators with an agreement term, <math id="A1.SS4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{m}s_{m}+\lambda\prod_{m}s_{m}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>m</mi></msub><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>m</mi></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∏</mo><mi>m</mi></msub><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>m</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{m}s_{m}+\lambda\prod_{m}s_{m}</annotation></semantics></math>, or a disagreement penalty, <math id="A1.SS4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{m}s_{m}-\lambda\,|s_{1}-s_{2}|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>m</mi></msub><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>m</mi></msub></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{m}s_{m}-\lambda\,|s_{1}-s_{2}|</annotation></semantics></math>; both reduce to summation at <math id="A1.SS4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda=0</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Summation has two useful properties, with empirical comparisons in Table <a href="#S4.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ 4.5 Training ablations ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> and Fig. <a href="#A2.F7" title="Figure 7 ‣ Training trajectories and aggregation operators. ‣ B.4 Additional measurements ‣ Appendix B Experimental Details and Additional Analyses ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>. First, multiplicative aggregation is sensitive to low scores: one near-zero score can suppress an expert regardless of the other routers’ scores. Summation does not impose this requirement for agreement. Second, with <math id="A1.SS4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{s}_{i}=\sum_{m}s_{m,i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>s</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>m</mi></msub><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{s}_{i}=\sum_{m}s_{m,i}</annotation></semantics></math>, the expert’s output gate in Eq. <a href="#S3.E3" title="In 3.2 Multi-Router: score aggregation before selection ‣ 3 Method ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> can be decomposed into per-router contributions, <math id="A1.SS4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{i}=\sum_{m}\alpha_{i}s_{m,i}/\sum_{j\in\mathcal{S}}\bar{s}_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>m</mi></msub><mrow><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em">/</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi></mrow></msub><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>s</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{i}=\sum_{m}\alpha_{i}s_{m,i}/\sum_{j\in\mathcal{S}}\bar{s}_{j}</annotation></semantics></math>. A product does not have this additive decomposition, and its scale depends on <math id="A1.SS4.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math>. The same raw sigmoid scores also supply the input-mixing weights in §<a href="#S3.SS3" title="3.3 Multi-View: router-conditioned expert inputs ‣ 3 Method ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a>: for each selected expert, its scores are normalized across routers, <math id="A1.SS4.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{m,i}=s_{m,i}/\sum_{n}s_{n,i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo rspace="0.055em">/</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>n</mi></msub><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{m,i}=s_{m,i}/\sum_{n}s_{n,i}</annotation></semantics></math>, so that <math id="A1.SS4.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{m}a_{m,i}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>m</mi></msub><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{m}a_{m,i}=1</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS4.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS4.p3.1" class="ltx_p">We also evaluate a variant that selects experts using <math id="A1.SS4.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\max_{m}s_{m,i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>max</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\max_{m}s_{m,i}</annotation></semantics></math> and gates their outputs using <math id="A1.SS4.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{m}s_{m,i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>m</mi></msub><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{m}s_{m,i}</annotation></semantics></math>. Selection therefore depends on an expert’s highest router score, while the output weight uses scores from all routers. This separates the effects of score aggregation on selection and gating. Conceptually, it corresponds to choosing one router at the selection stage, analogous to choosing one view for an expert’s input in a hard single-view variant. Table <a href="#S4.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ 4.5 Training ablations ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> separately reports the evaluated view-mixing variants.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.5 </span>Aggregation before selection</h3>

<div id="A1.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The layer aggregates all router scores before a single top-<math id="A1.SS5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> selection. Every router scores the full expert set <math id="A1.SS5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{1,\dots,N\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{1,\dots,N\}</annotation></semantics></math>, and the number of activated experts remains <math id="A1.SS5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>, independent of the number <math id="A1.SS5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> of routers or <math id="A1.SS5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> of views. All routing heads contribute to one shared ranking over the full expert pool.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">An alternative is to distribute a fixed budget of <math id="A1.SS5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> selections adaptively among routers. Although this preserves the total budget, each router still ranks experts independently and selects only up to its assigned quota. An expert may therefore be excluded from each local selection even if its aggregate score would place it in the global top-<math id="A1.SS5.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>. We instead aggregate the scores and perform one selection with a fixed total of <math id="A1.SS5.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> experts.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.6 </span>Cost accounting in detail</h3>

<div id="A1.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS6.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="A1.SS6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>L</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math> be the number of MoE layers. The hidden dimension is <math id="A1.SS6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math>, the latent dimension is <math id="A1.SS6.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math>, and there are <math id="A1.SS6.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> routed experts with <math id="A1.SS6.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> active per token. For the main configuration with <math id="A1.SS6.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=K</annotation></semantics></math>, each layer adds <math id="A1.SS6.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K-1</annotation></semantics></math> projections of shape <math id="A1.SS6.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d\times D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d\times D</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.SS6.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R-1</annotation></semantics></math> routing heads of shape <math id="A1.SS6.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D\times N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D\times N</annotation></semantics></math>. Thus,</p>
<table id="A1.E6" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_table">
<tbody>

<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.E6X.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=(K-1)D(d+N)," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=(K-1)D(d+N),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>

<tr id="A1.E6Xa" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
