<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.E6Xa.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=L\Delta\theta_{\mathrm{layer}}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>layer</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=L\Delta\theta_{\mathrm{layer}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS6.p1.3" class="ltx_p">With <math id="A1.SS6.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L=24" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>24</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L=24</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A1.SS6.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=2</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A1.SS6.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D=1024" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1024</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D=1024</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A1.SS6.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d=512" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>512</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d=512</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A1.SS6.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N=256" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>256</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N=256</annotation></semantics></math>, Multi-View adds <math id="A1.SS6.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="786{,}432" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>786,432</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">786{,}432</annotation></semantics></math> parameters per layer and <math id="A1.SS6.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="18{,}874{,}368" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>18,874,368</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">18{,}874{,}368</annotation></semantics></math> in total, approximately <math id="A1.SS6.p1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.19\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.19</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.19\%</annotation></semantics></math> of the 10B-parameter backbone. Multi-Router adds only the routing heads: <math id="A1.SS6.p1.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="262{,}144" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>262,144</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">262{,}144</annotation></semantics></math> parameters per layer and <math id="A1.SS6.p1.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6{,}291{,}456" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>6,291,456</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6{,}291{,}456</annotation></semantics></math> in total, approximately <math id="A1.SS6.p1.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.06\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.06</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.06\%</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS6.p2.2" class="ltx_p">The expert path still evaluates <math id="A1.SS6.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> unchanged experts on <math id="A1.SS6.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional inputs. For each token and layer, the additional projections and scoring matrices require <math id="A1.SS6.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(K-1)D(d+N)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(K-1)D(d+N)</annotation></semantics></math> multiply–accumulate operations (MACs). Counting one MAC as two FLOPs, and a direct mixture as <math id="A1.SS6.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> multiplications and <math id="A1.SS6.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K-1</annotation></semantics></math> additions per coordinate, the additional forward cost for <math id="A1.SS6.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K\geq 2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K\geq 2</annotation></semantics></math> is approximately</p>
<table id="A1.E7" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_table">
<tbody>
<tr id="A1.E7X" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<p id="A1.SS6.p2.3" class="ltx_p">The estimate covers scoring and projection matrix multiplications and input blending per token and layer. Expert-block FLOPs are unchanged. The implementation still dispatches <math id="A1.SS6.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> vectors of dimension <math id="A1.SS6.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math> per token, preserving all-to-all volume (App. <a href="#A1.SS7" title="A.7 Implementation ‣ Appendix A Extended Method Discussion ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.7</span></a>).</p>

<tr id="A1.T5.2.6" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="A1.T5.2.6.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;">Detached views</th>
<td id="A1.T5.2.6.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><math id="A1.T5.m10" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.00\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.00</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.00\times</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td id="A1.T5.2.6.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><math id="A1.T5.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="16{,}908" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>16,908</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16{,}908</annotation></semantics></math></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 5: </span>Same-cluster throughput in tokens/s/card for the listed 10B-A1B ablation configurations. Coupled and detached variants use view-fed scoring. Expert FLOPs are normalized to the backbone. Main-framework parameter counts are given in Eq. <a href="#A1.E6" title="In A.6 Cost accounting in detail ‣ Appendix A Extended Method Discussion ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS7" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.7 </span>Implementation</h3>

<div id="A1.SS7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Standard MoE implementations permute tokens before all-to-all communication, copying each token’s latent vector once per selected expert into a buffer organized by expert. Multi-View instead constructs the <math id="A1.SS7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional mixed input <math id="A1.SS7.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{v}_{i}=\sum_{m}a_{m,i}v^{(m)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>v</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>m</mi></msub><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>v</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{v}_{i}=\sum_{m}a_{m,i}v^{(m)}</annotation></semantics></math> for each selected (token, expert) pair on the token’s device before dispatch. For <math id="A1.SS7.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> tokens, the implementation flattens the <math id="A1.SS7.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T\times k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T\times k</annotation></semantics></math> token–expert slots, each with one selected expert as its destination. Each token still dispatches <math id="A1.SS7.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> vectors of dimension <math id="A1.SS7.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math>, so the all-to-all volume is unchanged. Dispatching all <math id="A1.SS7.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> views and combining them on the expert’s device would instead multiply that volume by <math id="A1.SS7.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math>. The return all-to-all communication, inverse permutation, and gated sum of expert outputs are unchanged.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS7.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS7.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Because selection uses no per-view quota, load balancing is applied once over the <math id="A1.SS7.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> experts using the backbone’s existing scheme. No auxiliary loss is added for the views.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS7.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS7.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The expert bias is added after summing the routing-head scores and is used only by top-<math id="A1.SS7.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> selection, <math id="A1.SS7.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}=\mathrm{TopK}_{k}(\bar{s}+b)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>TopK</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>s</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}=\mathrm{TopK}_{k}(\bar{s}+b)</annotation></semantics></math>; it enters neither the input-mixing weights nor the output gates. The output gates follow Eq. <a href="#S3.E3" title="In 3.2 Multi-Router: score aggregation before selection ‣ 3 Method ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>: the uncorrected <math id="A1.SS7.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{s}_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>s</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{s}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> are normalized over the selected set and then multiplied by the backbone’s per-expert output scale. For input mixing, Eq. <a href="#S3.E4" title="In Routing, mixing, and gating. ‣ 3.3 Multi-View: router-conditioned expert inputs ‣ 3 Method ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> normalizes each selected expert’s raw sigmoid scores across routers, and the resulting coefficients directly form <math id="A1.SS7.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{v}_{i}=\sum_{m}a_{m,i}v^{(m)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>v</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>m</mi></msub><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>v</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{v}_{i}=\sum_{m}a_{m,i}v^{(m)}</annotation></semantics></math>. The input-ratio computation uses <math id="A1.SS7.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon=10^{-9}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon=10^{-9}</annotation></semantics></math> for numerical stability, omitted from the mathematical formulas. At fixed parameters, replacing the score sum by its mean and scaling <math id="A1.SS7.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>b</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math> by <math id="A1.SS7.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1/R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>R</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1/R</annotation></semantics></math> preserves selection, output gates, and view weights. To maintain the bias correspondence during training, its initialization and update increments must also be scaled by <math id="A1.SS7.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1/R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>R</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1/R</annotation></semantics></math>. In Multi-Router, repeating one routing head <math id="A1.SS7.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> times and multiplying its balancing bias by <math id="A1.SS7.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> preserves the forward computation with a single routing head.</p>
</div>
<section id="A1.SS7.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Execution-path verification.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For the checkpoint probes, we verify the expert IDs, output gates, and mixing weights received by the dispatcher. Appendix <a href="#A2.SS6" title="B.6 Expert-input diversity and controlled mixing interventions ‣ Appendix B Experimental Details and Additional Analyses ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.6</span></a> reports these execution checks and identity-replay errors.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS8" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.8 </span>Interaction with other components</h3>

<div id="A1.SS8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Multi-View modifies the MoE down-projection, router, and permutation step. Attention, including multi-head latent attention (MLA) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">DeepSeek-AI et al., 2024a</a>)</cite>, is unchanged, as is the KV cache. Hyper-connections and their manifold-constrained variant mHC use multiple residual streams with learned mixing between sublayers <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhu et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xie et al., 2025</a>)</cite>. Multi-View accepts the resulting sublayer input <math id="A1.SS8.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math> and returns a <math id="A1.SS8.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional output, so these designs are architecturally compatible. Multi-token prediction (MTP) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">DeepSeek-AI et al., 2024b</a>)</cite> adds prediction modules and a loss term, while Multi-View leaves the training objective unchanged. In our configuration, the MTP module uses a dense FFN and is not modified. The method is also compatible in design with fine-grained and shared experts, auxiliary-loss-free balancing, and dense or hash-routed early layers <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">Roller et al., 2021</a>)</cite>. It leaves the vocabulary, embeddings, routed and active expert counts, expert blocks, up-projection, and expert-parallel layout unchanged.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS9" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.9 </span>Warm-starting from a LatentMoE checkpoint</h3>

<div id="A1.SS9.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS9.p1.1" class="ltx_p">An existing LatentMoE checkpoint provides a possible initialization for Multi-View. View 1 retains the checkpoint’s down-projection and routing head. The remaining views are initialized from the same projection with small perturbations, and their routing heads are initialized to zero. These additional routing heads add the same constant to every expert’s raw score, preserving the raw-score ordering but generally changing normalized output gates. Keeping the balancing bias <math id="A1.SS9.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>b</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math> unchanged also preserves the actual bias-corrected selection, because the same constant is added to every entry of <math id="A1.SS9.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{s}+b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>s</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{s}+b</annotation></semantics></math>. The views can then differentiate during continued training.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS10" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.10 </span>Properties: tied views and view differentiation</h3>

<section id="A1.SS10.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Tied-view reduction.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS10.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS10.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Since <math id="A1.SS10.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{m}a_{m,i}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>m</mi></msub><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{m}a_{m,i}=1</annotation></semantics></math>, tying all <math id="A1.SS10.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{m}=P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{m}=P</annotation></semantics></math> gives <math id="A1.SS10.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{v}_{i}=(\sum_{m}a_{m,i})Ph=Ph" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>v</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mo lspace="0em">∑</mo><mi>m</mi></msub><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>P</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{v}_{i}=(\sum_{m}a_{m,i})Ph=Ph</annotation></semantics></math> for every selected expert. With the same router scores, selected set, and output gates, this recovers Multi-Router with the shared input <math id="A1.SS10.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z=Ph" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z=Ph</annotation></semantics></math>. All routers continue to score the same expert pool, independently of whether the view projections are tied.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS10.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Expert-dependent mixing.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS10.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS10.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For a given token, mixing weights that vary across experts allow those experts to receive different inputs. If all selected experts share <math id="A1.SS10.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{m,i}=a_{m}(h)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{m,i}=a_{m}(h)</annotation></semantics></math>, then</p>
<table id="A1.Ex3" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A1.Ex3X"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.Ex3X.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\hat{v}_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>v</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\hat{v}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.Ex3X.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\sum_{m}a_{m}(h)\,P_{m}h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mi>m</mi></munder></mstyle><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\sum_{m}a_{m}(h)\,P_{m}h</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="A1.Ex3Xa"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.Ex3Xa.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\Big(\sum_{m}a_{m}(h)\,P_{m}\Big)h=P_{a(h)}\,h," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">(</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mi>m</mi></munder></mstyle><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>m</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\Big(\sum_{m}a_{m}(h)\,P_{m}\Big)h=P_{a(h)}\,h,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS10.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">All <math id="A1.SS10.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> experts then share an input, but <math id="A1.SS10.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{a(h)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>P</mi><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{a(h)}</annotation></semantics></math> can still vary with the token, so input modulation remains. When <math id="A1.SS10.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{m}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{m}</annotation></semantics></math> is constant, including <math id="A1.SS10.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{m}=1/K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{m}=1/K</annotation></semantics></math>, the mixture can be absorbed into a fixed projection. The main method’s <math id="A1.SS10.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{m,i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{m,i}</annotation></semantics></math> retains both token and expert dependence, providing modulation at this granularity without an additional mixing network.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS10.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Per-view load.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS10.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS10.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Aggregate load balancing (App. <a href="#A1.SS7" title="A.7 Implementation ‣ Appendix A Extended Method Discussion ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.7</span></a>) controls the number of tokens assigned to each expert, which affects dispatch cost and expert utilization. For the per-view diagnostics, let <math id="A1.SS10.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u_{m,i}(h_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>u</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u_{m,i}(h_{t})</annotation></semantics></math> denote the recorded weight of view <math id="A1.SS10.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math> at expert <math id="A1.SS10.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>. Define <math id="A1.SS10.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="p_{m,i}=\sum_{t:\,i\in\mathcal{S}(h_{t})}u_{m,i}(h_{t})\big/\sum_{j}\sum_{t:\,j\in\mathcal{S}(h_{t})}u_{m,j}(h_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.448em">:</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></msub><msub><mi>u</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em" rspace="0.055em" stretchy="true" symmetric="true">/</mo><msub><mo rspace="0em">∑</mo><mi>j</mi></msub><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.448em">:</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></msub><msub><mi>u</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{m,i}=\sum_{t:\,i\in\mathcal{S}(h_{t})}u_{m,i}(h_{t})\big/\sum_{j}\sum_{t:\,j\in\mathcal{S}(h_{t})}u_{m,j}(h_{t})</annotation></semantics></math> as the fraction of view <math id="A1.SS10.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math>’s recorded weight mass assigned to expert <math id="A1.SS10.SSS0.Px3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>. Aggregate assignment counts can remain unchanged while <math id="A1.SS10.SSS0.Px3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{m,\cdot}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">⋅</mo></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{m,\cdot}</annotation></semantics></math> varies. Different views can therefore concentrate on different subsets even when the aggregate expert load is uniform. We report the coefficient of variation of <math id="A1.SS10.SSS0.Px3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{m,\cdot}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">⋅</mo></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{m,\cdot}</annotation></semantics></math> and the effective expert count <math id="A1.SS10.SSS0.Px3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\exp(H_{m})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\exp(H_{m})</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A1.SS10.SSS0.Px3.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{m}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{m}</annotation></semantics></math> is the entropy of <math id="A1.SS10.SSS0.Px3.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{m,\cdot}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">⋅</mo></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{m,\cdot}</annotation></semantics></math> (App. <a href="#A2.SS7" title="B.7 Aggregate and per-view expert load ‣ Appendix B Experimental Details and Additional Analyses ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.7</span></a>). A low effective count indicates concentration on fewer experts. We also report the ratio of an expert’s selection share to its gate-mass share, which distinguishes changes in assignment frequency from changes in output weighting.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS10.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Differentiation.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS10.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS10.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The tied configuration <math id="A1.SS10.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{1}=\dots=P_{K}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">⋯</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>K</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{1}=\dots=P_{K}</annotation></semantics></math> is symmetric, but it is preserved by a gradient update only when the gradient components of the views coincide. Each <math id="A1.SS10.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{m}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{m}</annotation></semantics></math> receives gradients through the selected experts that assign nonzero mixing weight to view <math id="A1.SS10.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math>, scaled by <math id="A1.SS10.SSS0.Px4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{m,i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{m,i}</annotation></semantics></math> in Eq. <a href="#S3.E5" title="In Routing, mixing, and gating. ‣ 3.3 Multi-View: router-conditioned expert inputs ‣ 3 Method ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>. Because these weights can vary across experts and tokens, the views can receive different updates without an explicit diversity penalty. We assess router disagreement (§<a href="#S4.SS3" title="4.3 Router preferences shape expert computation ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.3</span></a>) and per-view load (App. <a href="#A2.SS7" title="B.7 Aggregate and per-view expert load ‣ Appendix B Experimental Details and Additional Analyses ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.7</span></a>).
The checkpoint probes in §<a href="#S4.SS3" title="4.3 Router preferences shape expert computation ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.3</span></a> measure mixing-weight and expert-input diversity. Controlled interventions in App. <a href="#A2.SS6" title="B.6 Expert-input diversity and controlled mixing interventions ‣ Appendix B Experimental Details and Additional Analyses ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.6</span></a> test whether the trained model uses the correspondence between experts, tokens, and mixtures.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix B </span>Experimental Details and Additional Analyses</h2>

<section id="A2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.1 </span>Full configuration</h3>

<div id="A2.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Appendix <a href="#A2.SS2" title="B.2 The 10B-A1B configuration ‣ Appendix B Experimental Details and Additional Analyses ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.2</span></a> gives the complete architecture and training configuration. The model has hidden dimension <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D{=}1024" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1024</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D{=}1024</annotation></semantics></math>, 24 layers, latent dimension <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d{=}512" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>512</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d{=}512</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N{=}256" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>256</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N{=}256</annotation></semantics></math> routed experts with top-8 selection and one always-active shared expert. Matrix parameters use Muon, while embeddings, the output head, biases, and router weights use AdamW. Training uses a warmup–stable–decay schedule with peak learning rate <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6\times 10^{-4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6\times 10^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math>, 4096-token sequences, approximately <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="7.9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>7.9</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7.9</annotation></semantics></math>M tokens per optimizer step, and BF16 with FP8 (E4M3) matrix multiplications under 8-way expert parallelism. Each variant in §<a href="#S4" title="4 Experiments ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> changes one experimental setting.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.2 </span>The 10B-A1B configuration</h3>

<div id="A2.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A2.T6" title="Table 6 ‣ B.2 The 10B-A1B configuration ‣ Appendix B Experimental Details and Additional Analyses ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> specifies the 10B-A1B latent-space MoE, with approximately 10B total and 1B activated parameters. This configuration is used for all main results, ablations, and diagnostics in §<a href="#S4" title="4 Experiments ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>.</p>

</span></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 6: </span>Architecture of the 10B-A1B model.</figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Attention.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Each layer uses multi-head latent attention (MLA) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">DeepSeek-AI et al., 2024a</a>)</cite> with 16 attention heads. Queries are compressed to rank 512, and keys and values share a rank-512 latent representation. Each attention head has 192 query–key dimensions without rotary embeddings, 64 decoupled rotary dimensions, and a 256-dimensional value. QK-normalization is applied, rotary embeddings use base <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>4</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{4}</annotation></semantics></math>, and the attention output is gated. The cache stores the 512-dimensional KV latent and the 64-dimensional rotary key for each token and layer.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">MoE.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">All 24 FFN layers are latent-space MoE layers <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Elango et al., 2026</a>)</cite>, with no preceding dense FFN layers. Each token is projected from <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D{=}1024" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1024</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D{=}1024</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d{=}512" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>512</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d{=}512</annotation></semantics></math>, and 8 of 256 routed experts are activated. Each routed expert is a latent-space SwiGLU FFN with intermediate dimension 1024; one shared expert with the same intermediate dimension is always active. Expert biases are updated at rate <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{-4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math> for load balancing <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2024a</a>)</cite>, and the auxiliary-loss coefficient is 0.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">MTP.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Following <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">DeepSeek-AI et al. (2024b)</a></cite>, one multi-token prediction module predicts one additional future token. Its FFN is a dense SwiGLU with intermediate dimension 5120. Its loss is added to the language-modeling loss with weight 0.3.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Training.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The sequence length is 4096 tokens, and the global batch contains 1920 sequences, or approximately 7.9M tokens per step. Matrix parameters use Muon <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2025a</a>)</cite> with momentum 0.95 and five Newton–Schulz steps. Embeddings, the output head, biases, and router weights use AdamW with <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta=(0.9,0.95)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.9</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.95</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta=(0.9,0.95)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon=10^{-15}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>15</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon=10^{-15}</annotation></semantics></math>. The learning rate reaches <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6\times 10^{-4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6\times 10^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math> after 1000 warmup steps and follows a warmup–stable–decay schedule ending at 0. Weight decay is 0.1, and gradients are clipped at 1.0. Training uses BF16 with FP8 (E4M3) matrix multiplications, 8-way expert parallelism, and seed 42. The main baseline, Multi-Router, and Multi-View comparisons use the 708B-token checkpoints; training ablations use a common checkpoint.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.3 </span>Comparability protocol</h3>

<div id="A2.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The loss differences are of order <math id="A2.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{-3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{-3}</annotation></semantics></math>, making configuration consistency particularly important. We use the following comparison protocol.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><em id="A2.SS3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Run-pair reference.</em> A pair of near-matched runs exhibits a systematic loss offset. Its observed difference provides an empirical reference for the ablation magnitudes in Table <a href="#S4.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ 4.5 Training ablations ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><em id="A2.SS3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Matched code and configuration.</em> Each variant uses a common code snapshot with one experimental setting changed. Comparisons use configurations recorded during training, including initialization and its scale, optimizer, schedule, and data order.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS3.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><em id="A2.SS3.p4.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Complementary diagnostics.</em> We report expert load and utilization (App. <a href="#A2.SS7" title="B.7 Aggregate and per-view expert load ‣ Appendix B Experimental Details and Additional Analyses ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.7</span></a>) alongside loss to characterize how the expert pool is used.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.4 </span>Additional measurements</h3>

<section id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Downstream protocol.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate the baseline, Multi-Router, and score-derived Multi-View checkpoints from training step 90K, corresponding to 708B tokens at 7.86M tokens per step, on the nine tasks in Table <a href="#S4.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 4.2 Downstream performance ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>. CMMLU <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, MMLU <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hendrycks et al., 2020</a>)</cite>, MMLU-Redux <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gema et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, MMLU-Pro <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2024b</a>)</cite>, and BBH <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">Suzgun et al., 2022</a>)</cite> use 5-shot prompts. GPQA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">Rein et al., 2023</a>)</cite> uses 10-shot prompts. These tasks are answered without chain of thought. HotpotQA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2018</a>)</cite>, SimpleQA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wei et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, and PreciseWikiQA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bang et al., 2025</a>)</cite> use 10-shot prompts with chain of thought and are scored by an LLM judge (DeepSeek-V4-Flash). Group means and the overall mean are unweighted.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Training trajectories and aggregation operators.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#S4.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ Training convergence. ‣ 4.2 Downstream performance ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> in the main text shows the training trajectories of the baseline, Multi-Router, and Multi-View through 708B tokens and their loss differences. Figure <a href="#A2.F7" title="Figure 7 ‣ Training trajectories and aggregation operators. ‣ B.4 Additional measurements ‣ Appendix B Experimental Details and Additional Analyses ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> compares the post-sigmoid fusion operators at the shared ablation checkpoint.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A2.F7" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2610.40577v2/fig_mr_operators.svg" id="A2.F7.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:476/415;" width="476" height="415"></object>

All evaluated variants improve over the single-router baseline. The shaded range shows the observed run-pair difference.</figcaption>

</section>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.5 </span>Router-score alignment</h3>

<div id="A2.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS5.p1.3" class="ltx_p">For a layer and a sampled token set <math id="A2.SS5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math>, let <math id="A2.SS5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> be the latent input of token <math id="A2.SS5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>. Evaluating all <math id="A2.SS5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N=256" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>256</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N=256</annotation></semantics></math> experts gives the normalized output-norm proxy</p>

<p id="A2.SS5.p1.4" class="ltx_p">The normalization removes each expert’s average output scale. Let <math id="A2.SS5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{t,i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{t,i}</annotation></semantics></math> be the score before balancing bias: the score from a single routing head for the baseline and the summed scores from all routing heads for Multi-Router. Correlation is computed over the <math id="A2.SS5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> experts for each token:</p>

<p id="A2.SS5.p1.5" class="ltx_p">Token values are averaged within each microbatch to obtain <math id="A2.SS5.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho_{\ell,p,b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho_{\ell,p,b}</annotation></semantics></math> for layer <math id="A2.SS5.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math>, rank <math id="A2.SS5.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>, and microbatch <math id="A2.SS5.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>b</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math>. With participating ranks <math id="A2.SS5.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{P}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{P}</annotation></semantics></math> and microbatches <math id="A2.SS5.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{B}_{\ell,p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{B}_{\ell,p}</annotation></semantics></math>, the layer and global averages are</p>
<table id="A2.E10" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_table">
<tbody>
<tr id="A2.E10X" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A2.E10X.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{P}|}\sum_{p\in\mathcal{P}}\frac{1}{|\mathcal{B}_{\ell,p}|}\sum_{b\in\mathcal{B}_{\ell,p}}\rho_{\ell,p,b}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi></mrow></munder></mstyle><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></munder></mstyle><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{P}|}\sum_{p\in\mathcal{P}}\frac{1}{|\mathcal{B}_{\ell,p}|}\sum_{b\in\mathcal{B}_{\ell,p}}\rho_{\ell,p,b},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="2" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equationgroup ltx_align_right">(10)</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A2.E10Xa" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A2.E10Xa.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\rho_{\mathrm{global}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>global</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\rho_{\mathrm{global}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A2.E10Xa.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\frac{1}{24}\sum_{\ell=1}^{24}\rho_{\ell}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>24</mn></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>24</mn></munderover></mstyle><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\frac{1}{24}\sum_{\ell=1}^{24}\rho_{\ell}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS5.p1.6" class="ltx_p">For layer-wise summaries, we match the two diagnostic exports by logged step and average the last 201 records available in both exports. Layer-wise bands show one standard deviation over these measurements.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.6 </span>Expert-input diversity and controlled mixing interventions</h3>

<section id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Evaluation protocol.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">All probes in this subsection use the score-derived two-view checkpoint at step 90K, the same checkpoint used in Table <a href="#S4.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 4.2 Downstream performance ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>. The main evaluation contains 256 held-out sequences of 4096 input tokens, giving 1,048,320 next-token predictions; the clean checkpoint’s NLL is <math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.17617" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2.17617</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.17617</annotation></semantics></math> nats/token. The layer scan uses 80 sequences, giving 327,600 predictions. No model parameters are updated.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A2.F8" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2610.40577v2/fig_mv_supplement.png" id="A2.F8.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/370;" width="476" height="370" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 8: </span>Additional analyses of the 708B-token Multi-View checkpoint. <span id="A2.F8.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(a)</span> Mean view-1 share <math id="A2.F8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{1,i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{1,i}</annotation></semantics></math> by expert, with expert ranks determined independently in each layer. <span id="A2.F8.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(b)</span> Agreement between the two routing heads on 256 sequences. <span id="A2.F8.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(c)</span> Single-view interventions on 80 sequences, with downstream routing recomputed; bands are pointwise 95% CIs. <span id="A2.F8.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(d)</span> Final-layer effects grouped by clean token-NLL quintile on 256 sequences. The x-axis indexes five groups with equal numbers of predictions; error bars show 95% intervals.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Diversity definitions.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For token <math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, let <math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> be its <math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=8</annotation></semantics></math> selected experts. The probe uses the main method’s actual mixing proportions, <math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{m,i}(t)=a_{m,i}(t)=s_{m,i}(t)/\sum_{n}s_{n,i}(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em">/</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>n</mi></msub><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{m,i}(t)=a_{m,i}(t)=s_{m,i}(t)/\sum_{n}s_{n,i}(t)</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{m}r_{m,i}(t)=1" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{m}r_{m,i}(t)=1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{2,i}(t)=1-r_{1,i}(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo The actual input to expert <math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math> is</p>

<p id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.3" class="ltx_p">The bands in Fig. <a href="#S4.F5" title="Figure 5 ‣ 4.3 Router preferences shape expert computation ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>(a) are the 25th–75th percentiles across tokens. Mean cosine similarity between the two views ranges from <math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.059" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.059</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.059</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.530" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.530</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.530</annotation></semantics></math> across layers. The median view-separation norm, divided by the mean of the two view norms, ranges from <math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.969" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.969</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.969</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.380" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.380</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.380</annotation></semantics></math>. The projections therefore produce distinct views at this checkpoint.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Expert preferences.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Fig. <a href="#A2.F8" title="Figure 8 ‣ Evaluation protocol. ‣ B.6 Expert-input diversity and controlled mixing interventions ‣ Appendix B Experimental Details and Additional Analyses ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>(a) shows each expert’s mean <math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{1,i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{1,i}</annotation></semantics></math> over tokens selecting it; experts are sorted independently within each layer. All 256 experts are observed in each layer. The within-token component accounts for <math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="84.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>84.8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">84.8</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="88.7\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>88.7</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">88.7\%</annotation></semantics></math> of the measured share variance, while grouping by expert ID explains <math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="28.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>28.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">28.0</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="73.4\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>73.4</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">73.4\%</annotation></semantics></math>. Across layers, top-8 Jaccard between routing heads ranges from <math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.039" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.039</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.039</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.211" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.211</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.211</annotation></semantics></math>, and top-1 agreement ranges from <math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.5\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.5</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.5\%</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="37.2\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>37.2</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">37.2\%</annotation></semantics></math> (Fig. <a href="#A2.F8" title="Figure 8 ‣ Evaluation protocol. ‣ B.6 Expert-input diversity and controlled mixing interventions ‣ Appendix B Experimental Details and Additional Analyses ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>(b)).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Interventions and uncertainty.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Expert permutation shuffles the view proportions among the eight selected experts of each token. Token permutation shuffles them among tokens selecting the same expert; <math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="99.96\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>99.96</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">99.96\%</annotation></semantics></math> of selected assignments are permutable. For each selected assignment, a replacement <math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{1,i}^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow><mo>′</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{1,i}^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> is implemented through the dispatcher channels <math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(g_{i}r_{1,i}^{\prime},g_{i}(1-r_{1,i}^{\prime}))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow><mo>′</mo></msubsup></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow><mo>′</mo></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(g_{i}r_{1,i}^{\prime},g_{i}(1-r_{1,i}^{\prime}))</annotation></semantics></math>. The output gate <math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> remains attached to the original assignment and is not permuted. Uniform mixing uses <math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(g_{i}/2,g_{i}/2)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(g_{i}/2,g_{i}/2)</annotation></semantics></math>; the two single-view interventions use <math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(g_{i},0)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(g_{i},0)</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(0,g_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(0,g_{i})</annotation></semantics></math>. View projections, expert parameters, the selected expert set, and output gates at the intervened layer are retained. All reported changes use paired predictions on the same sequences. For the final-layer permutation tests, we average three permutation seeds within each sequence and bootstrap sequences to obtain 95% CIs. Table <a href="#A2.T7" title="Table 7 ‣ Interventions and uncertainty. ‣ B.6 Expert-input diversity and controlled mixing interventions ‣ Appendix B Experimental Details and Additional Analyses ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> reports the final-layer results. The probe reports mean absolute changes in the view-1 share of <math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px4.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.408" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.408</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.408</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px4.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.117" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.117</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.117</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px4.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.331" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.331</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.331</annotation></semantics></math> for expert permutation, token permutation, and uniform mixing, respectively.</p>
</div>
