<section id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Execution and replay checks.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">On a 16-sequence execution-check subset, the dispatcher receives the same expert IDs across interventions; output gates differ by at most <math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.2\times 10^{-7}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.2</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.2\times 10^{-7}</annotation></semantics></math> in relative error, and the realized view proportions at the dispatcher differ from their intended values by at most <math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6.0\times 10^{-8}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>6.0</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6.0\times 10^{-8}</annotation></semantics></math>. Two clean passes agree exactly on 32 sequences. At layer 24, identity replay gives a mean NLL change of <math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.95\times 10^{-7}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2.95</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.95\times 10^{-7}</annotation></semantics></math> nats/token, with a 95% CI spanning zero, and a mean absolute token-level difference of <math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.14\times 10^{-5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.14</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.14\times 10^{-5}</annotation></semantics></math>. Using replay rather than the clean pass as the paired reference leaves the reported effects unchanged at the displayed precision.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">For shallower interventions, rounding-level changes can alter later top-<math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> decisions. At layer 1, identity replay changes the final-layer expert set for <math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px5.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6.3\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>6.3</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6.3\%</annotation></semantics></math> of tokens in the execution check. On the 80-sequence scan, its mean NLL change is <math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px5.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5.51\times 10^{-6}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>5.51</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5.51\times 10^{-6}</annotation></semantics></math>, with 95% CI <math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px5.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[-1.37,1.57]\times 10^{-4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1.37</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>1.57</mn></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[-1.37,1.57]\times 10^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math> nats/token. The scan estimates total effects with downstream routing recomputed. Its intervals use its own 80-sequence sample and are pointwise intervals for individual layers.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px6" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Single-view and token-group results.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Both single-view interventions increase NLL at every scanned layer (Fig. <a href="#A2.F8" title="Figure 8 ‣ Evaluation protocol. ‣ B.6 Expert-input diversity and controlled mixing interventions ‣ Appendix B Experimental Details and Additional Analyses ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>(c)); their final-layer effects on 256 sequences appear in Table <a href="#A2.T7" title="Table 7 ‣ Interventions and uncertainty. ‣ B.6 Expert-input diversity and controlled mixing interventions ‣ Appendix B Experimental Details and Additional Analyses ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>. Both branches contribute to prediction in this trained checkpoint. Fig. <a href="#A2.F8" title="Figure 8 ‣ Evaluation protocol. ‣ B.6 Expert-input diversity and controlled mixing interventions ‣ Appendix B Experimental Details and Additional Analyses ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>(d) groups predictions into equal-sized quintiles of clean token NLL, with 209,664 predictions per group. Expert permutation has its largest absolute effect in the highest-loss quintile (<math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.02936" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.02936</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.02936</annotation></semantics></math> versus <math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.00170" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.00170</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.00170</annotation></semantics></math> in the lowest). Uniform mixing gives a middle-quintile <math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px6.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math>NLL of <math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px6.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.00206" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.00206</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.00206</annotation></semantics></math>. The largest intervention effects occur in the highest-loss group.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS7" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.7 </span>Aggregate and per-view expert load</h3>

<div id="A2.SS7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Per-view load measurements show how each view’s recorded weight mass is distributed across the shared expert pool. Load balancing acts once on the aggregated assignment over the <math id="A2.SS7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> experts (App. <a href="#A1.SS7" title="A.7 Implementation ‣ Appendix A Extended Method Discussion ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.7</span></a>), so different views may concentrate on different subsets while the aggregate load remains balanced. We therefore report, for each view, the coefficient of variation (CV) of its recorded weight mass across experts and an effective expert count <math id="A2.SS7.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\exp(H_{m})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\exp(H_{m})</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A2.SS7.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{m}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{m}</annotation></semantics></math> is the entropy of this normalized weight mass (App. <a href="#A1.SS10" title="A.10 Properties: tied views and view differentiation ‣ Appendix A Extended Method Discussion ‣ Multi-View Latent MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.10</span></a>). The aggregate load CV is <math id="A2.SS7.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.854" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.854</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.854</annotation></semantics></math>, compared with <math id="A2.SS7.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.862" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.862</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.862</annotation></semantics></math> for the baseline, and the aggregate effective count is <math id="A2.SS7.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="188.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>188.7</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">188.7</annotation></semantics></math>, compared with <math id="A2.SS7.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="187.6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>187.6</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">187.6</annotation></semantics></math> out of <math id="A2.SS7.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="256" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>256</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">256</annotation></semantics></math>. The individual views have CVs of <math id="A2.SS7.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.155" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.155</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.155</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS7.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.144" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.144</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.144</annotation></semantics></math> and effective counts of <math id="A2.SS7.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="149.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>149.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">149.0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS7.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="150.2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>150.2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">150.2</annotation></semantics></math>. These counts correspond to approximately <math id="A2.SS7.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="58\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>58</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">58\%</annotation></semantics></math> of the pool for each view and <math id="A2.SS7.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="74\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>74</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">74\%</annotation></semantics></math> in aggregate. This pattern occurs across MoE layers (layer 2: <math id="A2.SS7.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="218" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>218</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">218</annotation></semantics></math> in aggregate versus <math id="A2.SS7.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="178" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>178</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">178</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS7.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="165" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>165</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">165</annotation></semantics></math>; layer 15: <math id="A2.SS7.p1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="159" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>159</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">159</annotation></semantics></math> versus <math id="A2.SS7.p1.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="123" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>123</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">123</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS7.p1.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="130" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>130</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">130</annotation></semantics></math>). Together, the views combine concentrated expert preferences with broader aggregate expert usage.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section><div class="ltx_rdf" about="" property="dcterms:creator" content="\ErnieAuthorNames"></div>
